lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: independence and the product rule

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: 30 people; 18 do A, 14 do B, 7 do both. Find P(A or B).

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An event has probability 7/9 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 18 successes and 43 failures; group Y with 16 successes and 44 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 7/10, P(B) = 4/10, and P(A and B) = 30/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).

items.prompt: In a group of 35, 16 do activity A, 13 do activity B, and 2 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 2/5 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: A survey table records: group X with 13 successes and 27 failures; group Y with 36 successes and 18 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Two events have P(A) = 3/10, P(B) = 8/10, and P(A and B) = 29/100. Are A and B independent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a group of 43, 15 do activity A, 30 do activity B, and 12 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
